[[Corey Burton]] |music= |timeline=[[22 BBY]]–[[19 BBY]]''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' }} '''''Star Wars: The Clone Wars''''' is an [[wikipedia:Animated_series|animated television series]] set between the events of [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars:'' Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']] and [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars:'' Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']]. The series aired on [[Cartoon Network]] for five seasons from [[2008]] to [[2013]], while an abridged sixth season was released through [[Netflix]] in [[2014]]. The final, [[The Clone Wars: Season Seven|seventh season]] was released on [[Disney+]] in [[2020]]. ==Development== [[File:LWF.jpg|thumb|left|250px|(left to right) George Lucas, Dave Filoni, and Catherine Winder discuss the series.]] [[George Lucas]] first had the idea for a [[Clone Wars]] animated series in [[2002]].{{WebCite|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/06/29/movies/29itzk.html|text=Free to Follow His Heart Right Back to 'Star Wars'|author=Dave Itzkoff|date=2008-06-29|archivedate=20181128222218}} ''[[Star Wars: Clone Wars]]'' aired on [[Cartoon Network]]{{SWArchive|url=clonewars/about/news/news20030220.html|text=Lucasfilm & Cartoon Network Announce: ''Star Wars: Clone Wars''}} from [[2003]] to [[2005]],{{SWArchive|url=clonewars/microseries/chapter/archive.html|text=''Clone Wars'' Chapter Archive}} produced by [[Genndy Tartakovsky]].{{SWArchive|url=clonewars/microseries/castcrew.html|text=''Clone Wars'' Cast & Crew}} Lucas then announced ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' at April 2005's [[Celebration III]], where he described ''Clone Wars'' as a "pilot television series" and said that ''The Clone Wars'' would "take that and turn it into a 3-D animated version full series."{{SWArchive|url=community/event/celebration/f20050419/indexp17.html|text=starwars.com at Celebration III - Thank the Maker: George Lucas}} [[Dave Filoni]] was hired as supervising director, and was familiar with previous ''Star Wars'' animation projects.{{WebCite|url=https://www.cbr.com/director-talks-star-wars-the-clone-wars|text=Director talks ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars''|author=Jami Philbrick|date=2008-10-07|archivedate=20200112170945}}{{WebCite|url=http://www.scifi.com/scifiwire/index.php?category=0&id=60272|text=Q&A: ''Clone Wars'' TV Show Revealed|author=Ian Spelling|date=2008-09-19|archivedate=20081216075906}} Filoni's initial idea for the series revolved around a recurring cast of characters who traveled aboard a spaceship similar to the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]''; the ship's crew would have included a smuggler, his girlfriend, a [[Gungan]] named Lunker, a [[Jedi]] [[padawan]] named Ashla, and her [[Jedi Master]]. This early concept for ''The Clone Wars'' was designed not to interfere with existing continuity, and as such would have included only occasional appearances from film characters, such as [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Anakin Skywalker]]. However, once Lucas became involved, he decided that the show would focus on the film characters, but would also include some of Filoni's ideas, such as Ashla (whose name was ultimately changed to [[Ahsoka Tano|Ahsoka]]).''[[The Art of Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' By [[February]] [[2006]], [[Lucasfilm Animation]] was working on animation tests and initial scripts, with Lucas playing a large part in the entire process.{{WebCite|url=http://www.movieweb.com/tv/news/90/11090.php|text=EXCLUSIVE INTERVIEW: Steve Sansweet Talks About the Upcoming ''Star Wars'' TV Shows!|author=Stephen Reedy|date=2006-02-15|work=[[Wikipedia:Valnet#MovieWeb|''MovieWeb'']]|archivedate=20080807173807}} The crew used [[Wikipedia:Autodesk|Autodesk]] [[Wikipedia:Software|software]] to animate both the film and the series. The [[Wikipedia:Maya (software)|Maya]] [[Wikipedia:3D modeler|3D modeling]] program was used to create highly detailed worlds, characters, and creatures.{{WebCite|url=http://usa.autodesk.com/adsk/servlet/item?siteID=123112&id=11774500&linkID=14271589|text=Autodesk Maya Software Serves as Animation Platform for New Star Wars: The Clone Wars Animated Feature Film and TV Series|date=2008-08-26|work=[[Wikipedia:Autodesk|Autodesk]] – Press Room Archive|archivedate=20171017002158|nolive=1}} Lucas and the animation team used this to create Zviz, a system that allowed the animation team complete freedom in framing shots.{{WebCite|url=https://www.awn.com/vfxworld/zviz-ilm-goes-interactive-previs|text=Zviz: ILM Goes Interactive with Previs|author=Barbara Robertson|date=2006-08-25|work=[[Wikipedia:Animation World Network|Animation World Network]]|archivedate=20200303013001}}{{WebCite|url=https://ew.com/tv/star-wars-the-clone-wars-dave-filoni-final-season-bad-batch-interview|text=''Clone Wars'' EP Dave Filoni breaks down the first episodes of the final season|author=Tim Leong|date=2020-03-02|archivedate=20200706084837}} Script, character design, and art direction were completed at [[Industrial Light & Magic|ILM]], with the animation and rendering done at [[Lucasfilm Animation Singapore]], and also [[Polygon Pictures]] between 2011 and 2013.{{WebCite|url=https://www.ppi.co.jp/works/star-wars-the-clone-wars|text=Star Wars: The Clone Wars|work=[[Polygon Pictures]]'s official website|archivedate=20240614083143}} No rotoscoping was involved, however, ILM did use motion capture. The final assembly of each episode was done at [[Skywalker Ranch]].{{WebCite|url=http://theforce.net/swtv/story/3D_Star_Wars_Cartoon_News_103405.asp|text=3D ''Star Wars'' Cartoon News|author=Dustin Roberts|date=2007-02-07|archivedate=20111129062941}} Lucas's involvement resulted in rewrites of most of the scripts, as Lucas insisted on more character development and that the show should not be based in one location, but as many as possible so as to make the story as interesting as possible to the viewer.{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/blogs/f20070831/index.html|text=Lucas Gets Involved}} The animation style was inspired by 1960s-era puppets-in-space serials such as [[Wikipedia:Gerry Anderson|Gerry Anderson's]] [[Wikipedia:Thunderbirds (TV series)|''Thunderbirds'']],August 11-24 issue of ''TV Guide'', ''The Clones Strike Back'' as well as the character designs from the original ''Clone Wars'' series.{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/blogs/f20071005/index.html|text=''Clone Wars'' Character Designer Kilian Plunkett}} Each episode of ''The Clone Wars'' was designed to be stand-alone, with an opening narration and moral to each story.{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/blogs/f20070803/index.html|text=Introducing Catherine Winder}} In terms of story and cinematography, the series was directed as if it were a live-action series, and the episodes were produced in widescreen.{{WebCite|url=http://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,20184842_2,00.html|text=George Lucas' 'Star Wars' plan|author=Joshua Rich|date=2008-03-18|archivedate=20130922062435}} Writer [[Henry Gilroy]] gained inspiration for the episode titles from the pulpy adventure sci-fi serials of the 1930s.[[Star Wars Insider 103|''Star Wars Insider'' 103]] The series utilized unused ideas from Lucas' previous ''Star Wars'' projects. [[Paul Dini]] pitched at least two rejected ideas for episodes: One involved [[Jar Jar Binks]] trying to convince the [[Galactic Senate]] that there is life on an obscure planet, and the other involved [[Anakin Skywalker]] and [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]] hiring an [[Ewok]] assassin.{{WebCite|url=http://smodcast.com/episodes/the-dini-dossiers-pt-1|text=Fat Man on Batman #017: Paul Dini: The Dini Dossiers Pt. 1|author=Kevin Smith|date=2012-11-21|work=[[Wikipedia:SModcast|''SModcast'']]|archivedate=20121202170728}} In 2008, In an interview they gave to TheForce.net, Filoni and Gilroy stated that, while Lucas gave them creative freedom for most of the series, there were several characters and locations that were off-limits. In respect to the characters, Lucas asked not to use [[Han Solo]], [[Chewbacca]], [[Boba Fett]], or [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure|Jabba the Hutt]] when Gilroy was writing the show bible, but by the time of the next meeting, Lucas had changed his mind about the latter two characters. In respect to the locations, Lucas asked Gilroy and Filoni to not explore the planets seen in the films, with the exception of [[Coruscant]]. But as with the character restrictions, he eventually changed his mind.{{WebCite|url=http://theforce.net/jedicouncil/interview/henrygilroyanddavefiloni.asp|text=Interviews | Henry Gilroy and Dave Filoni|date=2008-12-29|archivedate=20200608191740}} In the same interview, Filoni stated, “We could come up with ideas and present them to [Lucas] immediately, so there was no concern as to whether or not it “was” Star Wars. This series at least to George is NOT EU, it is a part of Star Wars as he sees it. I think if anything there was a period where Henry and I had to learn exactly what it took to be a part of George Lucas’ Star Wars, and tell the Star Wars story his way. We had to learn how to look at the Galaxy from his point of view and let go of some of what we considered canon after we found out the ideas were only EU. Really we had to “unlearn what we had learned” and go back to the movies as the defining source material.”  In the same year, in an interview featured in [[Star Wars Insider 103]], Gilroy explained, Lucas wanted “a process where he could be involved creatively at every step.” He and Filoni generated the initial 15 or so story ideas, developing them into premises, then met with Lucas for his input and approval, which was repeated with the final script for the story. As time went on, however, Lucas started to write his own story outlines for the writers to craft them into scripts. Gilroy said, “George is the Alpha and the Omega, and is involved in the story from beginning to end. On ''The Clone Wars'', that means from the initial story idea until the final sound mix” and that “just about every story now comes from ‘The Maker’ himself.”[[Star Wars Insider 103|''Star Wars Insider'' 103]] On [[March 11]], [[2013]], a video appeared on [[StarWars.com]], in which the crew explained that they were "winding down" the production of the series, and that they had finished the active production of new episodes.{{SW|url=news/a-new-direction-for-lucasfilm-animation|text=A New Direction for Lucasfilm Animation}} [[Lucasfilm Story Group]]'s [[Pablo Hidalgo]] stated that there years.{{SWArchive|url=community/event/celebration/news20070517b.html|text=First Look: ''The Clone Wars'' Celebration IV Poster}} Filoni and Winder also held similar presentations at [[Celebration Europe (2007)|Celebration Europe]] and WonderCon [[2008]].{{SWArchive|url=community/event/celebration/news20070627.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' at Celebration Europe}}{{SWArchive|url=community/event/con/news20080221.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' News Saturday at WonderCon}} StarWars.com created a new division of the site dedicated to ''The Clone Wars'', which was regularly updated with relevant content, including news articles, behind the scenes videos, and blog entries by [[Pete Vilmur]].{{OfficialBlog|url=2007/07/27/starwarscom-launches-the-clone-wars-section|text=StarWars.com Launches ''The Clone Wars'' Section}} ===Television=== Lucas shopped ''The Clone Wars'' to various networks, but had difficulty securing a buyer due to the show's unique tone.{{WebCite|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/entertainment/7048440.stm|text=Lucas begins ''Star Wars'' TV series|date=2007-10-17|archivedate=20200520060705}} Fox Broadcasting passed on it, and Cartoon Network was initially unsure. Several networks eventually got into a bidding war over the show.{{WebCite|url=http://blog.sfgate.com/tgoodman/2008/02/12/cartoon-network-lands-star-wars-the-clone-wars-tv-series-big-screen-movie-debuts-aug-15|text=Cartoon Network lands "Star Wars: The Clone Wars" TV series; big screen movie debuts Aug. 15.|author=Tim Goodman|date=2008-02-12|work=[[Wikipedia:SFGate|''SFGate'']]|archivedate=20171123044601}} [[Cartoon Network]] and [[Turner Network Television|TNT]] eventually won the broadcast rights, with [[Warner Bros.]] distributing a theatrical debut. Warner had tracked the series' development, and decided on a theatrical launch after viewing some footage.{{WebCite|url=http://variety.com/2008/digital/markets-festivals/animated-star-wars-to-hit-theaters-1117980757|text=Animated 'Star Wars' to hit theaters|author=Diane Garrett|date=2008-02-11|archivedate=20160123042209}} Stuart Snyder, former President of Cartoon Network, said he became interested in the new ''Clone Wars'' series immediately upon starting the job in May 2007. Snyder flew out to [[Wikipedia:San Francisco, California|San Francisco]], [[Wikipedia:California|California]] to screen several episodes, and told Lucas the only place he wanted to see the show was on Cartoon Network.{{WebCite|url=http://www.ajc.com/business/content/business/stories/2008/09/02/cartoon_clone_wars.html|text=Cartoon Network is eager to use the force|author=Kristi E. Swartz|date=2008-09-02|work=[[Wikipedia:The Atlanta Journal-Constitution|''The Atlanta Journal-Constitution'']]|archivedate=20080904044940}} It was announced on February 12, 2008 that the [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|feature film of the same name]] was to be released in theaters on August 15, 2008, with the TV debut in the fall.{{WebCite|url=http://www.usatoday.com/life/movies/news/2008-02-11-clone-wars-side_N.htm|text=New film, TV series fill in the 'Star Wars' blanks|author=Anthony Breznican|date=2008-02-11|archivedate=20081101151222}} This announcement was accompanied by an update of the Hyperspace online fan club kit,{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/fankit|text=Hyperspace Fan Club Kit}} and an offering of [[Rex|Captain Rex]] and [[Ahsoka Tano]] T-shirts to Hyperspace members.{{SWArchive|url=collecting/shop/shopnews/news20080212c.html|text=Exclusive ''Clone Wars'' Prelaunch T-shirt}}{{SWArchive|url=collecting/shop/shopnews/news20080212b.html|text=Hyperspace Exclusive Ahsoka T-shirt}} The series premiered on October 3, 2008 at 9 p.m. on the Cartoon Network. It aired on Friday nights{{WebCite|url=http://enewsi.com/news.php?catid=194&itemid=13013|text=Moving Forward, The Force Is With Cartoon Network|author=Jay Cochran|date=2008-04-04|work=[https://enewsi.com Entertainment News International]|archivedate=20080404144039}} as part of an [[Wikipedia:Action-adventure|action-adventure]] block alongside [[Wikipedia:The Secret Saturdays|''The Secret Saturdays'']] and [[Wikipedia:Ben 10: Alien Force|''Ben 10: Alien Force'']], in an attempt to rejuvenate the network and compete with channels, such as [[Wikipedia:Nickelodeon (TV channel)|Nickelodeon]] and the [[Disney Channel]]. Snyder expressed confidence that the shows would help boost ratings: "You catch me at a time where I have a smile on my face because of our internal results," Snyder said. "I can say there's a little bit of bragging on the third quarter for us." In Canada, the first season aired on [[Wikipedia:CTV Television Network|CTV]]{{WebCite|url=http://www.ctv.ca/servlet/ArticleNews/story/CTVNews/20080602/ctv_fallseason_080602/20080602|text=CTV fall season puts focus on Canadian fare|author=[[Wikipedia:The Canadian Press|The Canadian Press]]|date=2008-06-02|work=[[Wikipedia:CTV Television Network|CTV Television Network]]|archivedate=20090227024203}} and [[Wikipedia:Space (TV channel)|SPACE]], while the second through fifth aired on [[Wikipedia:Teletoon (Canadian TV channel)|Teletoon]], which aired repeats of the first season as part of its Weekday Action Force block. In Australia, the first season aired on Channel Ten. On April 13, 2011, ABC3 aired repeats of first season and has since aired seasons two, three, and four. During May 4-5, ABC3 did a marathon of all Season 5 episodes, which was the first time Season 5 had aired on ABC3. The series was first aired in the UK on [[Wikipedia:Sky Movies|Sky Movies]] Premiere and Premiere HD every Saturday at 5.30PM with the first episode aired on October 25, 2008. As with all programs on Sky Movies, it ran for the first 22-minutes of its 30-minute slot with advertisements shown at the end so as not to interrupt the episodes.{{WebCite|url=http://movies.sky.com/movie/the-clone-wars|text=Star Wars: The Clone Wars (TV)|work=[[Wikipedia:Sky Movies|Sky Movies]]|archivedate=20100502111302|nolive=1}}{{WebCite|url=http://www.jedinews.co.uk/misc/articles/star-wars-the-clone-wars-to-debut-on-sky-movies-premier|text=''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' to Debut on Sky Movies Premier|author=Adam Lamping|date=2008-09-26|archivedate=20181130122808}} Lucas expected ''The Clone Wars'' to run for four or five years, but planned to produce at least 100 episodes regardless of ratings.{{WebCite|url=http://www.comingsoon.net/movies/features/42983-exclusive-a-rare-sit-down-with-mr-george-lucas|text=Exclusive: A Rare Sit-Down with Mr. George Lucas|author=Edward Douglas|date=2008-03-17|work=[https://www.comingsoon.net ComingSoon.net]|archivedate=20180618184617}}{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/news/news20070309.html|text=Lucas Talks: ''Star Wars'' on Television}}{{WebCite|url=http://uk.ign.com/articles/2007/03/06/paley-fest-george-lucas-gives-details-on-the-star-wars-tv-shows|text=Paley Fest: George Lucas Gives Details on the ''Star Wars'' TV Shows|author=Eric Goldman|date=2007-04-05|archivedate=20190420181647}}{{WebCite|url=http://www.tvguide.com/news/lucas-wars-TV/070920-01|text=George Lucas, Episode II: ''Star Wars'' Strikes Back — on TV|author=Steve Sonsky|date=2007-09-20|work=[[Wikipedia:TV Guide|TV Guide]]|archivedate=20080921193236}} The first four seasons consisted of 22 episodes, the fifth of 20 episodes, and the sixth of 13 episodes. Lucasfilm told ''TV Guide'' that ''The Clone Wars'' would not supersede the original ''Clone Wars'' series in continuity, but would expand upon what the earlier series established. Dark Horse Comics editor [[Randy Stradley]] also claimed to have met with Lucasfilm Animation to discuss integrating the show with the [[Star Wars: Clone Wars (trade paperbacks)|''Clone Wars'' comics]].{{DHBoards|url=viewtopic.php?t=10498|thread=For Dark Horse Staff|nobackup=1}} However, the feature film and TV series introduced a number of continuity inconsistencies, many of which directly contradicted previously published sources and required [[Retroactive continuity|retcon]]s and major shifts in the previously established Clone Wars timeline which were never established by [[Leland Chee]].{{DHBoards|url=viewtopic.php?t=13886&postdays=0&postorder=asc&start=101|thread=''The Clone Wars'' continuity (Calling Mr. Chee)|nobackup=1}} There were several prominent examples of direct contradiction between ''The Clone Wars'' and previous ''Clone Wars'' media: *On [[August 8]], 2009, [[Star Wars: Republic Commando (novel series)|''Star Wars: Repbulic Commando'']] author [[Karen Traviss]] stated that she was leaving the ''Star Wars'' franchise due to alleged continuity issues raised with the publication of ''[[The Art of Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'',{{WebCite|url=http://karentraviss.typepad.com/blog/2009/08/end-of-one-era-start-of-another.html|text=End of one era, start of another…|author=Karen Traviss|date=2009-08-08|work=Karen Traviss's Blog|archivedate=20090810234747}} which included details regarding the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]] that clashed with the continuity set-up by her novels; this was most likely in reference to the trilogy of episodes involving [[Mandalore]] in the show’s second season ("[[The Mandalore Plot]]," "[[Voyage of Temptation]]" and "[[Duchess of Mandalore]]") in which the main Mandalorian faction is portrayed as a pacifist society living on Mandalore, which itself is portrayed as a radioactive desert, contradicting all previous descriptions.{{TCW|The Mandalore Plot}} Prior to the April 25, 2014, reorganization of canon, Leland Chee{{Twitter|HolocronKeeper|status/3221250171|[[Leland Chee]]|nobackup=1}} and [[Sue Rostoni]] maintained that the complications would eventually be worked-out.{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=270262&start=165#17701245|thread=Fan reactions- The Latest in Breaking News reactions- SPOILER WARNING!!!!!!|user=[[Sue Rostoni]]|date=2009-08-11|time=11:04 AM|quote=As for the rest, try not to get too caught up in it -- I don't think it's as huge an issue as is being played out. Not to belittle continuity at all -- that's not what I'm saying -- just have faith in Leland, et al, to work this out. We've always hinted that there will be continuity issues and that we'd have to wait until further along into the animated series to resolve them all, but it will work out.}} The two portrayals of the planet were reconciled with retcons issued by ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' and the subsequent ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: New Battlefronts: The Visual Guide]]'', which states that (much like Earth) the vast, white-sand deserts seen in the aforementioned episodes was but one region of the larger, varied landscape of Mandalore's surface. *The use of [[Eta-2 Actis-class light interceptor|Eta-2 ''Actis''-class interceptors]] at the same point in the timeline Anakin is knighted,{{CW|21}} whereas in ''The Clone Wars'' [[Delta-7B Aethersprite-class light interceptor|Delta-7B ''Aethersprite''-class light interceptors]] are used, which were ostensibly used before the later Eta-2s. In addition, some elements from works like the [[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|novelization of ''Revenge of the Sith'']] are being retconned. For example, in the novelization, Anakin remarks that he has only read about [[Grievous]]' [[IG-100 MagnaGuard]]s in an intel report, despite having fought them in the show.{{TCW|Duel of the Droids}} Another very noticeable continuity error is the fact that Anakin has his scar, which he received shortly after the [[Battle of Rendili]] from [[Asajj Ventress]]. He then injured Ventress so severely that she was forced to recuperate until the [[Battle of Boz Pity (Clone Wars)|Battle of Boz Pity]], after which she deserted the CIS and the war for good. However, he was originally shown to receive his scar in [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]], while the series begins in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]]. *In 2003, the reference book ''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Attack of the Clones]]'' established that Jedi Master [[Eeth Koth]] died during the [[First Battle of Geonosis]] when enemy fire brought down his gunship. However, the character was "resurrected" by the project; he was first mentioned as fighting in the Clone Wars in the 2008 novel ''[[The Clone Wars: Wild Space]]'' and was later featured prominently in the second-season episode "[[Grievous Intrigue]]." *The third season saw an evolution in the appearance of the main and supporting characters along with Ahsoka Tano's new attire representing a more mature look. Anakin Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi's attire was adjusted to be closer to how they appeared in [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Revenge of the Sith'']].{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/newcharacterlooks/index.html|text=A New Look for ''The Clone Wars'' Heroes}} *In the third season episode "[[Citadel Rescue]]," Jedi Master [[Even Piell]] died during a [[Battle of Lola Sayu|mission]] around the second year of the war. In the 2008 novel ''[[Coruscant Nights I: Jedi Twilight]]'', written by [[Michael Reaves]], [[Even Piell/Legends|Even Piell]] lived through the Clone Wars and died during the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]] in 19 BBY on Coruscant. *StarWars.com confirmed that Darth Maul survived the [[Battle of Naboo]] and would appear in [[The Clone Wars: Season Four|Season Four]] of the series.{{SWArchive|url=news/darth_maul_returns_2012.html|text=Darth Maul Returns to the Star Wars Saga This Spring!}} Maul returned in the [[Brothers (episode)|21st episode]], living on [[Lotho Minor]]. *The fifth-season opener "[[Revival (episode)|Revival]]" featured the death of Jedi Master [[Adi Gallia]] by Savage Opress [[Skirmish on Florrum|on]] [[Florrum]], despite having previously been slain by Grievous during the [[Battle of Boz Pity (Clone Wars)|Battle of Boz Pity]], one of the final battles of the Clone Wars in the 2005 comic [[Obsession 5|''Obsession'' 5]]. *The fifth season finale "[[The Wrong Jedi]]" presented that [[Barriss Offee]] fell to the [[dark side of the Force]] and [[Bombing of the Jedi Temple hangar|destroys]] the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] hangar, framing Ahsoka Tano, and [[Trial of Ahsoka Tano|initiating]] an investigation against Tano, but Anakin ultimately discovers her plot and Offee gets arrested and taken away to prison. However, the daily webstrips series ''[[Reversal of Fortune]]'' and the [[Databank (original)|Databank]] entry of [[Felucia]] originally stated that [[Barriss Offee/Legends|Barriss Offee]] was killed at the end of the Clone Wars during [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]] on [[Felucia/Legends|Felucia]], reflecting the original version of Order 66 in [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']], in which Offee was to die along [[Luminara Unduli]] and [[Shaak Ti]], whose death scenes were too omitted.{{WebCite|url=http://www.ccbanana.com/main/interviews/starwars1.htm|text=C.C. Banana Interviews the Stars of ''STAR WARS''!|work=[[Wikipedia:C.C. Banana|C.C. Banana]]|archivedate=20070512233219|nolive=1}} As Offee was depicted as still serving the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], it has been assumed in the Expanded Universe continuity that Offee remained at the Order through unknown reasons. Furthermore, Offee was intended to originally kill herself at the end of the episode, which would have contradicted her post-''The Clone Wars'' EU appearances definitively, but Dave Filoni cut the scene because he "had plans" for the character, which ultimately never came to fruition by the show's cancelation.{{SW|url=news/swca-the-untold-clone-wars-panel-liveblog|text=SWCA: The Untold ''Clone Wars'' Panel Liveblog}} *If the show had not been canceled, there was going to be an episode arc in the seventh season focusing on [[Maul]], which would have delved into his origins. While the episodes went unmade, their scripts were adapted into [[Dark Horse Comics]]' comic book series [[Star Wars: Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir|''Star Wars: Darth Maul—Son of Dathomir'']], which revealed [[Mother (title)|Mother]] [[Talzin]] to be Maul's mother, as well [[Savage Opress]]'. However, the novel ''[[Darth Plagueis]]'' had previously established that a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsister]] named [[Kycina]] was [[Darth Maul/Legends|Maul's]] mother, and the short story ''[[Restraint]]'' identified her as [[Savage Opress/Legends|Opress]]' mother as well. *One of the unproduced episodes due the show's cancelation would have featured the [[Yuuzhan Vong]], the extra-galactic species which first appeared in [[Del Rey]]'s [[1999]]-[[2003]] book series ''[[Star Wars: The New Jedi Order]]''. According to [[Pablo Hidalgo]], the episode wouldn't have specified the Vong's origins but only imply that they came from [[Yuuzhan Vong galaxy|another galaxy]], just as ''[[The New Jedi Order: Vector Prime]]'' originally established.{{Twitter|pablohidalgo|status/755516241083768833|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|quote=There were from 'elsewhere.' So, probably. Story never got into it.}} However, Hidalgo has stated that per George Lucas' vision of the Force, the Yuuzhan Vong weren't immune to the Force in the story.{{Twitter|pablohidalgo|status/755405799527243777|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|quote=@gudenruben @BFett_ @ZRIKEitter They weren't Force-immune in that story.}} This would have contradicted the EU, as the Yuuzhan Vong were established as immune to the Force (except to the [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]] and [[Odojinya|Force net]] attacks) in ''[[The New Jedi Order: Edge of Victory I: Conquest]]''. *Likewise, in a similar way to Barriss Offee and the Yuuzhan Vong, [[Jaime King]]'s husband, Kyle Newman has stated that there were several unfinished episodes planned for the sixth season of the show featuring [[Aurra Sing]], including one in which Sing was to be killed.{{YouTube|video=DU6WwLoQaqs|text=Solo Live Reaction|channel=channel/UCxnEDVUZe8-j61nKo4HzOYg|name=Steele Wars|quote=You know, she actually died befo... There were episodes of The Clone Wars season 6 that I was in, which were deleted and she was in that too and she died.}} Had this been canonized, it would have contradicted several of [[Aurra Sing/Legends|Aurra Sing's]] appearances in EU stories set during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] and the [[New Republic era|New Republic]] and [[New Jedi Order era]]s, precisely ''[[Coruscant Nights II: Street of Shadows]]'', ''[[Star Wars: Demolition]]'', and ''[[Legacy of the Force: Tempest]]''. Eventually, in the new Canon continuity Sing's fate was addressed in the [[Star Wars Anthology Series|''Star Wars'' Anthology]] film, ''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]'', in which it was established that [[Tobias Beckett]] pushed Sing to her death. Initially supervising director Dave Filoni defended any differences in continuity: "But there's never an implicit connection between the micro-series that Cartoon Network did previously and the series that we're doing now. I personally as a fan never think of it as discrediting any of the other material, it's just that other material is from a different point of view, a different look at the war and take on the war. It's an ever-Expanding Universe in a lot of ways."{{WebCite|url=https://www.cbr.com/director-talks-star-wars-the-clone-wars|text=Director talks ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars''|author=Philbrick, Jami|date=2008-10-07|archivedate=20200112170945}} At his Celebration IV presentations, Filoni showed a series of slides showing several character sculpture designs for the series—stating that they would share some of the stylization of the original ''Clone Wars'' series, but would also have some of the realistic look of the films. He explained, however, that elements of the series would differ slightly from what has been previously established in continuity.{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/blogs/news20070727b.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Celebration IV Panel -- Part 2}} Changes were made from the original ''Clone Wars'' series: Obi-Wan doesn't wear as much of his clone general armor, Grievous has a cough prior to the [[Battle of Coruscant]], and the Jedi fighting styles are more like the films, and not like some of the exaggerated Jedi abilities portrayed in the original series. Eventually Filoni would go on record to state that the Expanded Universe and ''The Clone Wars'' television series "don't live in the same universe".{{InsiderCite|134|Behind and Beyond the Battle Lines}} ''The Clone Wars'' was classified as [[Canon|T-canon]] in the [[Holocron continuity database]].{{Twitter|HolocronKeeper|status/402147701795463168|[[Leland Chee]]}}{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=152583&start=01755#17147721|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Tasty Taste]]|date=2008-02-20|time=4:19 PM}} However, on [[April 25]], 2014, it was announced that the Expanded Universe was to be re-branded as ''Star Wars'' Legends and that the only past material that would be considered canon would be the [[original trilogy]] and [[prequel trilogy]] films and ''The Clone Wars,'' while also enshrining Episodes 1-6 and The Clone Wars as the immovable truth for both timelines, thus negating any concerns regarding conflicts between the series and past ''Star Wars'' Legends material for content that was produced in the Canon timeline. Novelizations based on the series, however, are not considered canon, nor are video game releases or comics, with the exception of Legacy material and any other upcoming projects based on material that was developed for the television series that ultimately did not make it to broadcast.{{SW|url=news/the-legendary-star-wars-expanded-universe-turns-a-new-page|text=The Legendary Star Wars Expanded Universe Turns a New Page}}{{SW|url=news/sdcc-2014-star-wars-a-new-dawn-panel-liveblog|text=SDCC 2014: ''Star Wars: A New Dawn'' Panel – Liveblog}} Reference works based on the series, such as ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Character Encyclopedia]]'', are considered part of the "Legends" continuity and are not considered canon sources, albeit a canonical [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Character Encyclopedia - Join the Battle!|reference titles]] now exist for the series' characters. The '''first season''' of the animated ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series premiered on [[October 3]], 2008, with the airing of the episodes "[[Ambush]]" and "[[Rising Malevolence|Rising ''Malevolence'']]" on [[Cartoon Network]]. Four episodes were originally intended to be part of the first season, but they were instead combined and released as a feature animated film, [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'']], on August 15, 2008.

{{Top|rwm|can|fotj|title=''The Clone Wars'': Season Five}} {{TelevisionSeason |image=[[File:TCWs5WhoWillFall.jpg]] |title=''The Clone Wars'': Season Five |series=''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' |format=Animated |num episodes=20 |runtime=*Approx. 27 minutes per episode *9 hours 2 minutes
(542 minutes) {{C|total}} |network=[[Cartoon Network]] |first aired=[[September 29]], [[2012]] |last aired=[[March 2]], [[2013]] |creators=[[George Lucas]] |writers= |directors= |executive producers= |production company= |starring= |timeline=[[20 BBY]]–[[19 BBY]]''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' |preceded by=[[The Clone Wars: Season Four|''The Clone Wars'': Season Four]] |followed by=[[The Clone Wars: The Lost Missions|''The Lost Missions'']] }} {{Quote|Some of the characters that we have created for the show will meet their destinies.|Dave Filoni|{{InsiderCite|134|Behind and Beyond the Battle Lines}}}} '''''The Clone Wars'': Season Five''' was the fifth season of the animated ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series, which debuted on [[September 29]], [[2012]]. The season was first confirmed to be in development in [[December]] [[2011]]. Unlike the series' four previous seasons, which aired on Friday nights in prime time at 9:00 p.m. ET, Season Five aired on Saturday mornings at 9:30 a.m. ET.{{WebCite|url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2012/08/25/star-wars-the-clone-wars-season-5-trailer-reveals-premiere-date-a-new-timeslot-and-an-awesome-sith-battle|text=Star Wars: The Clone Wars - Season 5 Trailer Reveals Premiere Date, a New Timeslot and an Awesome Sith Battle!|author=Goldman, Eric|date=2012-08-24|quote=The end of the trailer also revealed both The Clone Wars premiere date and its new timeslot: Season 5 will premiere on September 29th, as the show moves from Friday nights to Saturday mornings at 9:30am.|archivedate=20161026230023}}{{WebCite|url=http://www.examiner.com/review/a-review-of-the-clone-wars-season-5-premiere|text=A review of The Clone Wars Season 5 premiere! - National Star Wars|author=Young, Bryan|date=2012-08-24|work=Examiner.com|quote=The Clone Wars is moving to a new time slot with that premiere: Saturday mornings at 9:30 am.|archivedate=20151031020617}} Also unlike previous seasons, Season Five consisted of only twenty episodes.{{WebCite|url=http://tvlistings.zap2it.com/tvlistings/ZCProgram.do?sId=EP01087361&t=Star+Wars%3A+The+Clone+Wars&method=getEpisodesForShow&desc=on|text=''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide|work=Zap2it|archivedate=20170120202320}}{{WebCite|url=http://www.teletoonmedia.com/en/index.php/teletoon/highlight/category/february_2013_programming_highlights|text=FEBRUARY 2013 PROGRAMMING HIGHLIGHTS|work=Teletoon|archivedate=20130104183445}} It was the final season of the series to be broadcast on [[Cartoon Network]]. Before it began airing, Hasbro suggested that Season Five would be the last season of ''The Clone Wars''.{{WebCite|url=http://www.jeditemplearchives.com/content/modules.php?name=News&file=article&sid=10434|text=Hasbro Q And A - MORE Of Your Questions Answered!|author=Paul|archivedate=20171202073820}} Supervising Director Dave Filoni disputed this claim at the time,{{SW|url=news/100-episodes-of-the-clone-wars-a-reflection|text=100 Episodes of ''The Clone Wars'': A Reflection}} and in [[Star Wars Insider 137|''Star Wars Insider'' 137]], he reiterated his intention to keep making the series as long as people were watching. He also announced that his staff had begun working on scripts and designs for a sixth season.{{InsiderCite|137|Star Wars: The Clone Wars Cast and Crew on...}} However, the series was canceled after Season Five, with thirteen remaining episodes that had been in development being released as [[The Clone Wars: The Lost Missions|The Lost Missions]] on [[March 7]], [[2014]].{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-clone-wars-the-lost-missions-now-on-netflix|text=Star Wars: The Clone Wars – The Lost Missions Now on Netflix|nolive=1}} In the fourteenth episode, "[[Eminence (episode)|Eminence]]," Cartoon Network censored the scene when [[Savage Opress]] decapitates several [[Black Sun]] [[Black Sun ruling council/Legends|leaders]]. However, it was confirmed that the full scene would be visible on the Blu-ray edition of the series. A scene from "[[Shades of Reason]]" was also censored, when [[Darth]] [[Maul]] decapitates [[Pre Vizsla]], and his head rolls down on the stairs of the throne room of [[Sundari Royal Palace/Legends|Sundari Royal Palace]]. ==Continuity== [[File:YodaMakeover-TCWs5BR2.png|thumb|right|400px|[[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] received an updated CG character model for Season Five (right)]] At one point, the "younglings arc" (i.e. "[[The Gathering (episode)|The Gathering]]," "[[A Test of Strength]]," "[[Bound for Rescue]]" and "[[A Necessary Bond]]") was considered as the pilot for a possible spin-off series.{{WebCite|url=http://www.cinemablend.com/television/1589720|text=The Last Star Wars Project George Lucas Considered Before Selling To Disney|author=Venable, Nick|date=2016-11-25|work=Cinema Blend|archivedate=20170802181114}} Under this plan,[[Star Wars Year by Year: A Visual Chronicle (updated edition)|''Star Wars Year by Year: A Visual Chronicle, Updated Edition'']] "[[A War on Two Fronts]]" was intended to be the Season Five premiere,{{InsiderCite|134|Launchpad}} though it was eventually changed to "[[Revival (episode)|Revival]],"{{InsiderCite|135|Launchpad}} with "A War on Two Fronts" becoming the second episode of the season. Following the episode order published in ''Insider'' 134, [[Star Wars Insider 137|''Star Wars Insider'' 137]] also reported the episodes through episode fifteen: {|{{Prettytable}} ! Episode !! The '''sixth season''' of the animated ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series, marketed as '''''The Clone Wars: The Lost Missions''''' was originally intended to be a full 22-episode season, but just thirteen episodes were completed following the series' retraction from [[Cartoon Network]] in [[March]] [[2013]]. The Lost Missions debuted on the German TV network [[Wikipedia:Super RTL|Super RTL]], airing between [[February 15]] and [[March 8]], [[2014]]. Following the announcement of an exclusive licensing agreement with [[The Walt Disney Company|Disney]] and the [[ABC Television Network|ABC Television Group]], [[Netflix]] released The Lost Missions on [[March 7]], 2014, exclusively to audiences in the United States and Canada.

==Development==
{{Quote|I've written, like, twelve, sixteen [episodes] now? Because we're three years ahead of you guys. We've already written Season Six.|Christian Taylor, in September 2011|<ref name="ForceCast S4 Premiere" />}}
In [[September]] [[2011]], then–head writer [[Christian Taylor]] stated that they had already written through Season Six.<ref name="ForceCast S4 Premiere">{{WebCite|url=http://forcecast.net/story/home/Special_Report_Clone_Wars_Season_4_Premiere_Part_II_140988.asp|text=ForceCast.net: Special Report: Clone Wars Season 4 Premiere, Part II|work=ForceCast.net|archivedate=20190419012740}}</ref> The sixth season had begun production by [[October]] [[2012]], when Series Supervising Director [[Dave Filoni]] confirmed that his crew had begun working on scripts and designs for the season in [[Star Wars Insider 137|''Star Wars Insider'' 137]].<ref name="Insider 137: TCW Crew">{{InsiderCite|137|Star Wars: The Clone Wars Cast and Crew on...|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' Cast and Crew on...}}</ref> Voice actor [[Stephen Stanton]] revealed that he had done "extensive" voice work for Season Six as of an interview with " Star Wars Book Report," in which Stanton and the podcast crew looked back on the first one hundred episodes of the series.<ref name="ShinyRobot">{{WebCite|url=https://bigshinyrobot.com/star-wars/interview-stephen-stanton/
|text=INTERVIEW: Stephen Stanton|work=bigshinyrobot.com|archivedate=20260104182057}}</ref>

==Release and reception==
{{Quote|We have wrapped production on all of the remaining Star Wars: The Clone Wars episodes, and while that might be sad news in one way, it's good news in another. It means you will finally get to see them. When, exactly, is a detail I cannot yet share. I can confirm that in early 2014 you will be watching the final episodes of The Clone Wars, including one of Master Yoda's most challenging missions.|Dave Filoni, in October 2013|<ref name="Filoni Season 6" />}}
[[Lucasfilm]] announced on [[March 11]], [[2013]]—following the series' [[The Clone Wars: Season Five|fifth season]] [[The Wrong Jedi|finale]]—that active production on future episodes for [[Cartoon Network]] had ceased, but that the studio was continuing production on as yet unreleased story arcs. In the weeks following the announcement, clips were shown from episodes that would have been part of Season Six and will still be released, despite the series being pulled from Cartoon Network.<ref name="New Direction">{{SW|url=news/a-new-direction-for-lucasfilm-animation|text=A New Direction for Lucasfilm Animation}}</ref> During the "Secrets of ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars''" panel at [[Celebration Europe II]], Filoni implied the small possibility that Season Six might end up being shown on television in the future.<ref name="SW-SWCE 2013: Opening Day Highlights">{{SW|url=news/swce-2013-friday|text=SWCE 2013: Opening Day Highlights|nolive=1}}</ref>

On [[October 11]], 2013, Filoni announced that his crew had completed production on the remaining ''The Clone Wars'' episodes and that they would be released in early [[2014]].<ref name="Filoni Season 6">{{Facebook|username=DaveFiloni|url=DaveFiloni/posts/10151886663275053|name=[[Dave Filoni]]|date=2013-10-11|quote=''Star Wars'' fans - I have some exciting news!|archiveurl=https://archive.is/REqWJ}}</ref>

On [[January 16]], 2014, the German television network [[Wikipedia:Super RTL|Super RTL]] announced that it would be airing episodes of the series' "sixth season" on Saturdays, beginning on [[February 15]] with four new episodes and continuing into the coming weeks.<ref name="German TV Schedule" /> On [[February 13]], 2014, [[StarWars.com]] announced that the series' thirteen final episodes would be released as "The Lost Missions" on [[Netflix]] in the United States and Canada on [[March 7]], as part of a deal that also included the series' [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|feature film]] and first five seasons.<ref name="TCW on Netflix" /> The "[[Launchpad]]" department in [[Star Wars Insider 148|''Star Wars Insider'' 148]] revealed the English names for the episodes as well as plot summaries and credits.<ref name="Launch Pad" />

The Lost Missions debuted on Netflix on March 7 at 12:01 am PT.<ref name="Jedi News-March 4">{{WebCite|url=http://www.jedinews.co.uk/misc/articles/the-clone-wars-the-lost-missions-arrives-on-netflix-at-1201am-pst-march-7th|text=Jedi News - Latest: ''The Clone Wars'' 'The Lost Missions' Arrives on Netflix at 12:01am PST March 7th|work=JediNews|archivedate=20190419012755}}</ref><ref name="Tumblr">{{Tumblr|subdomain=starwars|url=post/78483923558/prepare-your-queues-for-the-clone-wars-the-entire|name=Star Wars|text=Prepare your queues for The Clone Wars! The entire series, including The Lost Missions of season 6 come to Netflix at 12:01am PST, March 7th!}}</ref>  Coinciding with the Netflix launch, StarWars.com released official episode guides to accompany each of the final season's thirteen episodes.<ref name="TCW on Netflix" />

Beginning on [[June 9]], 2014, The Lost Missions became available on seven additional online formats, including [[Wikipedia:iTunes|Apple iTunes]] in the US and Canada, [[Wikipedia:Amazon.com|Amazon]], [[Wikipedia:Google|Google]] in the US and Canada, [[Wikipedia:Microsoft|Microsoft]] in the US and Canada, [[Wikipedia:Sony|Sony]] in the US and Canada, [[Wikipedia:Verizon Communications|Verizon]], and [[Wikipedia:Vudu|Vudu]].<ref name="Facebook 6/9/2014">{{Facebook|username=StarWarsTheCloneWars|url=StarWarsTheCloneWars/photos/a.350962014943099.76071.328988200473814/734710846568212|name=''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]''|date=2014-06-09|quote=We're excited to announce that The Clone Wars: The Lost Missions are now available on the following platforms: Apple iTunes (US & Canada), Amazon, Google (US & Canada), Microsoft (US & Canada), Sony (US & Canada), Verizon, VUDU|nobackup=1}}</ref> The episodes were released on [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars – The Lost Missions|Blu-ray and DVD]] on [[November 11]], 2014.<ref name="Home Video">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-clone-wars-the-lost-missions-blasts-onto-blu-ray-and-dvd|text=''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' - The Lost Missions Blasts Onto Blu-ray and DVD}}</ref>

I'm happy for the opportunity to define these things and the end of this part of the Clone War.|Dave Filoni| }} '''''The Clone Wars'': Season Seven''' was the seventh season of the animated ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series.{{Instagram|username=lucasfilm|url=p/BwSFXVqgeDJ|name=[[Lucasfilm]]|date=2019-04-15|quote=Loving the new poster art and trailer for Season 7 of #TheCloneWars, coming to #DisneyPlus!|archivefile=File:Season_7_poster_art_instagram.png}} Marketed as '''''The Final Season''''', it is a revival run of twelve episodes that aired on [[Disney+]]. The revival was announced by the series' supervising director, [[Dave Filoni]], on [[July 19]], [[2018]] at San Diego Comic-Con, during a panel commemorating the show's tenth anniversary. The episodes are a continuation of the series after it was cancelled in [[2013]], and include the [[Siege of Mandalore]]. Series stars [[Matt Lanter]], [[Ashley Eckstein]], [[James Arnold Taylor]], [[Dee Bradley Baker]], [[Tom Kane]], [[Sam Witwer]], [[Katee Sackhoff]], and more all returned to lend their voices to the series. ==Development== {{Quote|Without getting too much into detail - because I love the fan speculation - but it would be a real shame to have done all this work and not use it. So we are looking at everything and going over all those scripts we had. I think that the biggest thing for me is "how do we make this show better?" And I think that means examining all the work we had done, the work we were planning on doing, and also trying to honor the work of so many people that were in the middle of making stuff.|[[Dave Filoni]]|{{WebCite|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2018/08/12/star-wars-rebels-season-4-finale-clone-wars-final-season-revival-disney-dave-filoni|text=Star Wars Rebels Creator Dave Filoni Reveals How Season 4 Almost Ended and His Clone Wars Revival Plans|author=Huver, Scott|date=2018-13-08|work=[[Wikipedia:IGN|IGN]]|archivedate=20180812202220}}}} ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' ran from [[October 3]], [[2008]]{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode001.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Ambush}} until its final regular broadcast episode on [[March 2]], [[2013]],{{SW|url=explore/the-clone-wars/ep520|text="The Wrong Jedi" - ''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide|nolive=1}} following the show's cancellation at the end of its [[The Clone Wars: Season Five|fifth season]].{{SW|url=news/a-new-direction-for-lucasfilm-animation|text=A New Direction for Lucasfilm Animation}} A [[The Clone Wars: The Lost Missions|half-length season]] was available on Netflix on [[March 7]], [[2014]],{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-clone-wars-the-lost-missions-now-on-netflix|text=Star Wars: The Clone Wars – The Lost Missions Now on Netflix|nolive=1}} and [[The Clone Wars Legacy|some story arcs]] were released in several different mediums in the following years.{{SW|url=tv-shows/the-clone-wars-legacy|text=''The Clone Wars'' Legacy}} The show was succeeded by ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]'',{{SW|url=news/new-animated-series-star-wars-rebels-coming-fall-2014|text=New Animated Series Star Wars Rebels Coming Fall 2014}} which continued the story of [[Clone Wars]] era characters like [[Ahsoka Tano]] and [[Clone Captain]] [[Rex]],{{Rebels|Relics of the Old Republic}} but fans continued asking for more episodes of ''The Clone Wars''.{{SW|url=news/sdcc-2018-12-things-we-learned-from-the-star-wars-the-clone-wars-panel|text=SDCC 2018: 12 Things We Learned from the ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' Panel}} A famous hashtag for the campaign was ''#SaveTheCloneWars''.{{Twitter|username=SaveCloneWars|name=The Clone Wars: Season Seven|archivedate=20160703151733}} [[File:Star_Wars_The_Clone_Wars_revival_poster.png|thumb|left|250px|''The Clone Wars Saved'' poster]] An extension of the original series on the [[Disney+]] streaming service was announced at San Diego Comic Con on [[July 19]], [[2018]], during a panel commemorating the show's 10th anniversary. The announcement came with a trailer for the new season and a poster that contained the hashtag ''#CloneWarsSaved'', referencing the fan campaign. A [[StarWars.com]] interview with [[Dave Filoni: Clone Ranger!|Dave Filoni]], the show's supervising director, confirmed that the new season would contain 12 new episodes. One of the story arcs in the season was the [[Siege of Mandalore]], with some scenes about it in the trailer. The arc was originally intended as the show's series finale,{{Twitter|BFree63|status/654689846171070464|[[Brent Friedman]]|quote=It's a reference to Clone Wars' 'lost' series finale, since that arc and last night's ep were both written by @MattMichnovetz|archivefile=File:Friedman-LostSeriesFinale.png}} and takes place days before and during the events of [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']], including [[Order 66]].[[Ahsoka (novel)|''Ahsoka'']] The arc was referenced in ''Star Wars Rebels''{{Rebels|The Lost Commanders}} and partly adapted in the young-adult novel [[Ahsoka (novel)|''Ahsoka'']]. The author [[E. K. Johnston]] later revealed that she was asked not to write action scenes for the Siege of Mandalore in the book, as unbeknownst to her Lucasfilm was working on the final season.{{WebCite|url=http://www.starwarsreport.com/2019/04/18/live-at-celebration-with-e-k-johnston-swbw-100|text=Live at Celebration with E.K. Johnston – SWBW #100|date=2019-04-18|archivedate=20190824053633}} [[Matt Lanter]], [[Ashley Eckstein]], [[James Arnold Taylor]], and [[Dee Bradley Baker]] were confirmed to be reprising their respective roles as [[Anakin Skywalker]], Ahsoka Tano, [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], and [[Captain]] Rex by the revival trailer. In August 2018, [[Tom Kane]] confirmed on his [[Wikipedia:Facebook|Facebook]] account that he had recorded lines for five new episodes of the revival, but he did not confirm if he would be reprising his roles as either the Narrator, [[Yoda]], or [[Wullf Yularen]]. He went on to reprise all three roles.{{TCW|Old Friends Not Forgotten}}{{TCW|Shattered}} As of [[November 5]], 2018, recording was still underway according to Eckstein.{{WebCite|url=https://www.cbr.com/star-wars-clone-wars-season-7-ashley-eckstein-interview|text=Star Wars: The Clone Wars' Ashley Eckstein Offers an Update on Season 7|author=Damore, Meagan|date=2018-11-05|archivedate=20190716032913}} [[Sam Witwer]] and [[Ray Park]] were later confirmed to be reprising the role of [[Maul]], with the former providing the voice as he had done in previous seasons and the latter performing motion capture reference.{{WebCite|url=https://www.looper.com/201596/the-truth-about-darth-mauls-clone-wars-return-exclusive|text=The truth about Darth Maul's Clone Wars return – Exclusive|author=Gates, Christopher|date=2020-04-14|archivedate=20200420180745}} During production, several of the models, including that of Captain Rex, were tweaked and improved upon based on new animation technology. [[Star Wars Insider 190|''Star Wars Insider'' 190]] later revealed that as of [[June 12]], [[2019]], production of the episodes was still ongoing.[[Star Wars Insider 190|''Star Wars Insider'' 190]] Filoni felt that his experience making ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]'' had informed his work on this season.{{WebCite|url=https://io9.gizmodo.com/how-star-wars-the-clone-wars-long-hiatus-and-the-mand-1841833402|text=How ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' Long Hiatus, and ''The Mandalorian'', Made It Even Better|author=Lussier, Germain|date=2020-02-24|archivedate=20200224195118}} Even though he was no longer working on the franchise, ''[[Star Wars]]'' creator [[George Lucas]] talked about some series concepts and ideas with Filoni, who endeavored to keep the revival with Lucas' vision so it, along with other projects, could be faithful to the franchise's films and ideologies.{{WebCite|url=https://www.indiewire.com/2020/02/star-wars-the-clone-wars-dave-filoni-interview-1202212493|text='Star Wars: The Clone Wars': Dave Filoni Discusses the Final Eps and George Lucas's Ongoing Mentorship|author=Hersko, Tyler|date=2020-02-20|archivedate=20200221020128}} ==Release and reception== ''The Clone Wars'' revival was the subject of a panel at [[2019]]'s [[Celebration Chicago]], which took place on [[April 14]].{{SW|url=news/animation-panels-at-star-wars-celebration-chicago|text=Lucasfilm To Host Three Animation Panels at ''Star Wars'' Celebration Chicago}} During the panel, behind-the-scenes images and a trailer were shown. The trailer, besides showing more footage of "Ahsoka's Walkabout" and the Siege of Mandalore also confirmed that the revival would include a finished version of the "Bad Batch" arc, initially released as an unfinished story reel, with completed animation. [https://www.heruniverse.com Her Universe] released a new line of clothing based on Season Seven.{{SW|url=news/rundisney-star-wars-rival-run-weekend-themes-revealed-exclusive|text=runDisney ''Star Wars'' Rival Run Weekend Themes Revealed! - Exclusive}} The season premiered on [[Disney+]] on [[February 21]], [[2020]].
